summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR696 crore (+22% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 27.2%, and FY27 margin guidance raised 200 bps to 27% ±2%.
summary.overview: Garware Hi-Tech Films reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR696 crore, up 22% YoY and 10% QoQ, with EBITDA up 42% YoY to INR189 crore at a 27.2% margin (+377 bps YoY). PAT rose 42% to INR129 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,329 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR381 crore (+49%) and PAT INR262 crore (+50%). Management raised FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 27% ±2% and reaffirmed revenue above INR2,500 crore, while flagging a ~INR37 crore headwind from raw material and logistics costs in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Management calls ~30% a sustainable Q1 seasonal level

financial_highlights.value: CPD 73%, IPD 27%; value-added products 86% of revenue

segments.name: Sun Control Film (SCF)
segments.commentary: 51% of Q2 revenue. Utilisation 75% in Q2; management expects full utilisation by Q2 FY28. Market leader with 60-65% share in India.

segments.name: Paint Protection Film (PPF)
segments.commentary: 24% of Q2 revenue. Utilisation 73% in Q2, expected near 90-100% within about 6-12 months. Claims 60% share of Indian market; India PPF penetration ~3% of new cars.

segments.name: IPD (industrial products)
segments.commentary: About 25% of Q2 revenue, but only 10-12% margin per management; treated as a support business for CPD films.

segments.name: Architectural / window films
segments.commentary: About 30% of window film sales, annualised ~INR400 crore; target to reach INR1,000 crore. Management targets 35-40% growth for architectural in the US.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (D2C studios)
segments.commentary: Studios grew from 9 in Q1 to 14 in Q2, with 12 more planned in Q3 and a target of 50 by December 2027. Revenue targets INR50 crore, INR100 crore, INR200 crore over about three years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised 200 bps to 27% ±2% (earlier 25% ±2%); FY27 revenue target reaffirmed at more than INR2,500 crore.
Management indicated FY28 revenue of INR3,000 crore plus; analyst's INR3,100-3,200 crore figure was not confirmed ('exact number I can't quote').
FY28 margin expected to rise 1.5-2% from TPU backward integration; management said FY28 margin would be at least 28%, with 28-28.5% targeted.
Medium-term FY28-31 margin guidance of 27%+ plus 150-200 bps from TPU integration, as per presentation.
Full capacity potential of about INR3,500 crore once the TPU line and new SCF line are running.
Targets of 25-30% CAGR for both exports and domestic; each segment to grow at least 20%.
Q3 expected to be seasonally low, with Q4 recovering.
capex_capacity: TPU film line on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27; expected to supply about 25% of output externally (INR75-100 crore in FY28) and 75% captive for PPF.

INR191 crore solar control film capacity expansion focused on architectural and robotics; commercial production expected H1 FY28 (around June 2027), adding about 1,200 lakh sq ft of fungible capacity and INR450-500 crore revenue potential.
Past six capex programmes in six years totalled about INR500 crore, all internally funded. Further capex over the next three years is under consideration; no board approval yet.
PPF line about one year old; a fungible capacity can shift SCF lines to PPF if demand rises.
Lubrizol strategic MOU for aliphatic TPU technology and resins; TPU EBITDA margin estimated at about 35%.
demand_pricing: Q2 geography: export 80% and domestic 20%; US 51%, Europe 15%, India 20%, rest (Middle East and nearby) 12%.
Raw material costs rose about 4% QoQ, and logistics costs rose INR9 crore; total headwind about INR37 crore in Q2.
Management says pricing is passed through to customers in IPD; for CPD, crude correlation is 10-12% for SCF and 5-7% for PPF, with a maximum of about 15%.
Global price positioning: architectural products now at 85-120% of global peers, up from 30-40% earlier.
Architectural: raised prices and added products; EBITDA margin on top SCF products 40-45%, mid-range SCF 30-35%, PPF 20-25%.

Tariff reversal: INR31 crore received to date (INR20 crore refunded to customers, INR11 crore booked); a further ~INR30 crore expected in Q3 (INR16 crore to books, INR14 crore to customers). Reported by reducing COGS and sales.
Inventory raised intentionally: raw materials to protect against supply disruption; export inventory days up 15-25 at customers; total 58-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing capacity, and the product mix behind it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full utilisation of the TPU and SCF capacities could reach about INR3,500 crore; the new SCF line contributes INR450-500 crore and PPF can add about INR250 crore from current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration (reported as 30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Concentration exists, with one large EV customer in the US under long-term agreement; management says growth is spread across teams and that this customer does not buy architectural films.

qa_highlights.question: Crude sensitivity and the revenue impact at USD60 crude?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD100-110 crude, management said it passes through costs with a lag. Revenue would have been about INR650-660 crore instead of INR700 crore at USD60, with the lower-crude benefit mainly on the 25% crude-linked IPD business.

qa_highlights.question: Lubrizol tie-up structure and incremental top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Lubrizol supplies TPU resins and development support; 75% of TPU output goes captive into PPF (1.5-2% margin gain), and 25% goes to the market for INR75-100 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Home-solutions studio target and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets of INR50 crore, INR100 crore and INR200 crore are multi-year, not one-year; D2C adds about 10-15% to margins over the roughly 40% top architectural products.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would convey the shareholder request to the board, citing large upcoming capex.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: one large customer, with other customers 'half that size' or one-third; management says agreements are in place.
Crude and raw material cost volatility; Q2 headwind about INR37 crore; pass-through is partial and slow for CPD.
Geopolitical disruption and the Middle East slowdown; inventory build (58-60 days) ties up working capital.
Anti-dumping duty on Chinese PPF imports was approved by the Ministry of Commerce but not by the Finance Ministry; follow-up action pending.
Execution risk on TPU commissioning (Q3 FY27), the SCF line (H1 FY28), and the 50-studio D2C rollout by December 2027.
A regulatory penalty of INR25 lakh from MPCB for consent validation, linked to an old boiler run during trials.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, margins and capacity, with forward targets stated firmly. Evasive on specifics where management preferred not to commit: FY28 revenue ('exact number I can't quote'), future capex (not board-approved), and the medium-term margin framing, which was clarified only under follow-up questioning.
key_quotes: We delivered our highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR696 crores, up 22% year-on-year and 10% sequentially, which is nearing the INR700 crores mark.
As our product mix evolves, we believe margins of around 30% in Q1 represents a sustainable seasonal level.
Reflecting this confidence, we have upgraded our FY27 EBITDA margin guidance by 200 basis points to 27% plus-minus 2% while reaffirming our revenue target of more than INR2,500 crores.
We are the frontrunner having 60% of market size with us, rest goes to imports.
So, right now, we are 80% to 85% of the global player.

TPU film line, ~25% sold externally (INR75-100 crore FY28), 75% captive for PPF

growth.why: FY27 revenue held at more than INR2,500 crore (H1 at INR1,329 crore, +25%) with EBITDA margin guidance raised to 27% ±2%; backing is partly specific (TPU line Q3 FY27, INR191 crore SCF expansion around June 2027, 12 studios planned Q3) but the revenue path to INR2,500 crore lacks a stated order book or capacity bridge.
